title: UN report: world lacks realistic pathway to meet 1.5°C warming limit
summary: A September 2, 2026 UN Environment Programme report concluded the world has no realistic pathway to meet the 1.5°C warming limit set by the Paris Agreement. Current emissions of 40 billion tonnes yearly will exhaust the remaining 130-billion-tonne carbon budget in roughly three years.
takeaways: Remaining CO2 budget from 2026 onward: 130 billion tonnes
Current emissions: ~40 billion tonnes per year
Exceeding 1.5°C now characterized as "unavoidable" by IPCC lead author
Human-induced warming: nearly 1.4°C, rising ~0.25°C per decade
World headed for 2.6°C warming by century's end under current policies
Three-in-four probability 2026–2030 mean will breach 1.5°C target

takeaways: Additional warming by 2100: 0.2°–0.4°C (0.4°–0.7°F) from natural feedback loops
